description: TOP, LIMIT [OFFSET] and the ANSI FETCH over a twenty-row fixture. LIMIT takes the first n of an ordered result and OFFSET skips before it, which is enough to page through the whole table four rows-of-five at a time; an offset beyond the data answers nothing and a partial last page answers what remains. TOP n is the same thing written in front of the select list - with a WHERE, with a descending order, over an aggregate, and larger than the table, where it answers every row. FETCH FIRST / FETCH NEXT n ROWS ONLY agree with both, and ROWS is optional. LIMIT 0 answers nothing, OFFSET 0 changes nothing, and all three forms apply AFTER grouping and HAVING, so a limited aggregate is a limit on the GROUPS. Converted 1:1 from query/TopLimitTest (now retired); the Java read the first and last rows by walking the ResultSet cursor, so each converted test pins the whole ordered row set - which is what actually shows a page's boundaries rather than just its size. The fixture's twenty rows are built with a GENERATOR scan instead of the Java loop's twenty INSERT statements.
